 Daniel Craig lookalike slashes £750,000 off £3 million asking price of 11,000 sq ft James Bond-inspired Skyfall mansion featuring rare 007 memorabilia, Aston Martin blueprints and film props 
 Daniel Craig lookalike slashes £750,000 off £3 million asking price of 11,000 sq ft James Bond-inspired Skyfall mansion featuring rare 007 memorabilia, Aston Martin blueprints and film props 
 TOI Real Estate Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Nov 16, 2026, 21:56 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Daniel Craig lookalike Dean Reep reduces the asking price of his James Bond-inspired mansion. (Photo: Rightmove) A James Bond enthusiast who transformed his sprawling mansion into a 007-inspired paradise has been forced to slash its asking price by £750,000 after struggling to find a buyer willing to pay the original £3 million. Entrepreneur Dean Reep, who reportedly bears a striking resemblance to former James Bond actor Daniel Craig, spent years turning his six-bedroom luxury property in Retford, Nottinghamshire, into a tribute to the iconic spy franchise. Aptly named Skyfall, the 11,000 sq ft mansion is filled with rare James Bond memorabilia, signed photographs, film props and bespoke interiors inspired by the movies. However, despite its extraordinary collection and lavish features, the property has failed to attract a buyer at its original asking price, according to The Daily Mail. The mansion was listed for £3 million last year. Following price reductions in July and September, Reep is now inviting offers exceeding £2.25 million. James Bond-inspired mansion features rare 007 memorabilia and film props
 The luxury property houses rare James Bond memorabilia spanning generations of the franchise. (Photo: Rightmove) The property is home to an extensive collection of James Bond memorabilia spanning several generations of the franchise, from Sean Connery and Roger Moore to Daniel Craig. Among its standout pieces are Sir Roger Moore's gold-plated Seiko watch from Moonraker, rare Aston Martin DB5 blueprints and several items associated with the production of Skyfall and Quantum of Solace. The mansion's interiors have been carefully designed to recreate the atmosphere of the Bond films. Visitors are welcomed by two enormous stag sculptures at the electric gates, inspired by those outside Bond's ancestral home in the 2012 film Skyfall. Inside, giant portraits depicting memorable scenes from the franchise adorn the walls. The metal railings around the bay windows are also replicas of those seen at Bond's apartment in Spectre. The master suite features several pieces of film-related memorabilia, including a leather chair from Spectre, M's chair and stunt jackets associated with Quantum of Solace and Skyfall. From Bond-themed cocktail bar to private gym and tennis court: A look inside the £2.25 million property
 Inside Skyfall, the £2.25 million James Bond-inspired mansion with an extraordinary collection of 007 memorabilia. (Photo: Rightmove) The 11,000 sq ft residence offers much more than its impressive collection of movie memorabilia. It features a Bond-themed cocktail bar, a games room and a full-size snooker area, giving the property the feel of a private entertainment club. The luxury facilities also include a private gym, steam room and spa-style bathroom. Outside, the mansion boasts a sweeping driveway, a triple garage and a Wimbledon-inspired tennis court with an adjoining pavilion. Estate agents Fine & Country have described the six-bedroom residence as a 'truly exceptional private residence'. In its sales brochure, the agency states, 'Skyfall represents one of the most distinctive homes to come to the market in Nottinghamshire. Combining architectural grandeur, bespoke craftsmanship and a design narrative inspired by the world of James Bond, this remarkable estate offers a lifestyle rarely found within a single residence.' Who is Dean Reep? Entrepreneur bought the mansion for £750,000 in 2017
 From rare film props to Aston Martin references, every corner of the Skyfall mansion celebrates the iconic spy franchise. (Photo: Rightmove) Dean Reep, a 53-year-old entrepreneur and father, purchased the property for £750,000 in 2017 and subsequently spent years transforming it into a James Bond-inspired residence. He runs several businesses, including a technology firm, and has even established a company called Universal Exports Worldwide Ltd, a reference to the fictional organisation used as a front for MI6 in the James Bond films. Reep was also previously reported to own an Aston Martin DBS featuring a personalised 007 number plate, further reflecting his fascination with the fictional British secret agent.  The luxury residence combines cinematic inspiration with lavish amenities, including a steam room and private gym. (Photo: Rightmove) Despite the reduction in its asking price, the property continues to be marketed as an unusual luxury residence with a distinctive cinematic identity. The estate agents have highlighted that its appeal goes beyond its size and lavish specifications, with the carefully curated collection making it a celebration of one of cinema's most recognisable franchises. The sales listing states, 'Skyfall is unique not simply because of its size or specification, but because of the extraordinary story behind it.' It further highlights the rare signed artefacts, Aston Martin references, film-set pieces and production memorabilia connected to legendary Bond actors and movies. While the mansion may offer the experience of living inside a James Bond film, its reduced asking price suggests that finding a buyer with the same passion for the iconic spy franchise has proved more challenging than creating the ultimate 007-inspired home.
